title: Fourfold Displays for 'ggplot2'
text: fourfold display special case radial diagram, “polar area chart”, designed \(2 \times 2\) (\(2 \times 2 \times k\)) tables (Fienberg, 1975; Friendly, 1994a, 1994b). frequency \(n_{ij}\) cell shown quarter circle whose radius proportional \(\sqrt{n_{ij}}\), area proportional cell count. Like pie chart, uses segments circle show frequencies; unlike pie chart, keeps angles segments constant varies radius. \(2 \times 2\) cousin graphic form used Florence Nightingale (Nightingale, 1858). Friendly & Andrews (2021) describe rich history radial diagrams. main purpose display show sample odds ratio. gives number compares odds event (accepted!) happening one group (men) odds happening another group (women). \[ \hat{\theta} = \frac{n_{11} / n_{12}}{n_{21} / n_{22}}              = \frac{n_{11} \, n_{22}}{n_{12} \, n_{21}} . \] association two variables (\(\theta \neq 1\)) appears tendency one pair diagonally opposite cells larger pair. fourfold plot shows association odds ratio visually follows: Color diagonal tick marks show direction association: relatively larger diagonal pair drawn blue (expected independence) tick marks along diagonal, pair red. Confidence rings around quadrant give visual test independence, \(H_0: \theta = 1\): standardized display, rings adjacent quadrants overlap observed counts consistent null hypothesis.

Now rings upper quadrant overlap quadrant odds ratio differ 1.  default, margin = c(1, 2), standardizes margins. four quadrants align horizontally vertically odds ratio 1, regardless marginal frequencies, association admission gender can seen without influence overall admission rate numbers men women applied. fully standardized display usually useful form.  quadrants align, 95% confidence rings, computed interval \(1.62 \le \theta \le 2.09\), overlap: odds ratio differs significantly 1, apparent evidence gender bias favour men.
